description:
FILED s518d resume #2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-17) from the s518d board diff: Capture-Tiny 13-stdout-tied.t / 14-stderr-tied.t / 23-all-tied.t now RUN to near the end (they died at the *PLAN* before; s518d's #3203 / #3208 / #3372 got them there), and most of their newly reached fails are THIS bug.
With STDOUT tied (t/lib/TieLC: a class whose PRINT lower-cases into its own handle opened ">&=STDOUT"), `capture { ... }` captures through the TIE where perl captures the descriptor: Capture::Tiny's `$localize{stdout}++, local(*STDOUT), _open(\*STDOUT, ">&=1") if $do_stdout && tied *STDOUT` (Capture/Tiny.pm:344) is meant to give the capture an untied STDOUT on fd 1.
Minimal: scratch/s518d/pr/tlc2.pl
  use lib ".../Capture-Tiny-0.50-0/lib", ".../t/lib"; use TieLC; use Capture::Tiny qw/capture/;
  open my $save, ">&STDOUT"; tie *STDOUT, 'TieLC', ">&=STDOUT";
  my ($o) = capture { print STDOUT "STDOUT:Hello World" };
  my ($o2) = capture { system($^X, '-e', 'print STDOUT q{STDOUT:Hi There}') };
  untie *STDOUT; open STDOUT, ">&", $save; print "[$o] [$o2]\n";
perl 5.40.3: [STDOUT:Hello World] [STDOUT:Hi There]
PCL (efdaf775): the child's text reaches the TERMINAL, then [stdout:hello world] [] -- the in-process print went through the tie (lower-cased), the child's fd 1 was never redirected.
NOT #3370: rewriting those three Capture::Tiny lines so the `local(*STD..)` term LEADS the statement (a copy of the dist, scratch/s518d/ct-copy) leaves 13/14/15 at exactly the same pass/fail counts.  Next step: probe `tie *STDOUT ...; { local *STDOUT; open STDOUT, ">&=1"; open STDOUT, ">&" . fileno($tmp); print ...; system ... }` alone vs perl (the localized STDOUT and the later _open_std reopen onto the capture file).
Board rows citing it (s518d): the lc'd-output and empty-output rows of 13 / 14 / 23 (counts in the s518d board edit).


=== DONE (s519b, two of three causes; the third is #3370) ===
Commit 9dd184fd (rebased a67219b0): (1) a bare `local *STDOUT` (any forced-main name) inside a non-main package now localizes *main::STDOUT (Pl/Parser.pm forces the name to main as its other uses are) -- before, it localized a package-local STDOUT and the tie stayed in force inside Capture::Tiny's capture; (2) `*A = *STDOUT` / `local *A = *STDOUT` alias the standard handle (`%p-glob-io-key`): `print A` wrote NOTHING before, silently (pre-existing).  Guard Pl/t/tiehandle-01.t rows 27-28 (fail on fca3593b).
The third cause is #3370 (s519a: the comma-list `local (*STDOUT, ...)` term).  Real dist on s519b: 13-stdout-tied.t 631 / 208, 14-stderr-tied.t 661 / 212, 23-all-tied.t 560 / 284 = the blessed round-1 counts (one-file runs, s520).  A copy of the dist with the `local` hoisted (= #3370 simulated, scratch/s519b/ctdist + rewrite-ct.pl) reads 744 / 129 with no lower-cased or empty capture row left (the rest = #3326 unicode 104 + #3327 merged order).  NO board row edited: they move at the round board after s519a merges.  Docs: ir-spec "handles", tie-aggregates §7.
Bars (s519b final): gate PASS, sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18,748 (+0), corpus-diff = the #3405 :body token only.
Status stays OPEN until #3370 lands and the round board shows the capture rows move (Fable).


=== DONE (s519b, s520 second resume: the third cause #3370 is on main) ===
Acceptance on the s519b tree rebased onto MAIN-READY-29 (#3370 in), one-file runs: Capture-Tiny 13-stdout-tied.t 631/208 -> 744/129, 14-stderr-tied.t 661/212 -> 744/129, 23-all-tied.t 560/284 -> 747/130 (= the s519 simulation's 744/129).  No lower-cased or empty capture row is left.  baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv EDITED (0690d7dc): 322 rows left, 252 still-failing rows re-caused to #3326 (unicode bytes, 210) / #3327 (merged order, 42), 4 newly reached last rows "STD{OUT,ERR} is still tied" filed as #3434 (pre-existing on main).  The duplicate-fix reconciliation with s519a's #3411 kept main's Pl/Parser.pm rule; this task's runtime half (%p-glob-io-key, `*A = *STDOUT` aliases the real handle) stays; tiehandle-01.t rows 27-28 and local-term-01.t both pass in the gate (323 files / 10,988 rows).
subject: Capture::Tiny under a TIED STDOUT/STDERR: capture { } records the tie's output (lower-cased by t/lib/TieLC) and a child's output escapes to the terminal; perl captures the descriptor
